finding_key: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts::`get /start` is single-use and method-agnostic, so any duplicate/speculative request silently breaks the login for 30s
evidence: Verified against the supplied packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts: the /start branch checks only url.pathname, never req.method, and sets startConsumed on the first request of any kind, so a HEAD/prefetch/scanner/duplicate-open request burns the one-time 302 and the real navigation gets 410. With no /callback, the 30s timeout then rejects with the generic 'Login timed out' message (sawUnboundCallback is false), giving no hint the link was consumed. Single-use is an intentional security tradeoff, but the method-agnostic consumption and the undiagnosed benign-duplicate failure are real; impact is an intermittent, recoverable login hang with a misleading error, so I rate it minor.
